examples.title: Example 1: Switching the Background Color with a Modifier
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to switch the background color of a Button component by binding it to a modifier.

examples.title: Example 2: Implementing the Pressed State Effect with a Modifier
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to implement a pressed state effect for a Button component by binding it to a modifier. For details about how to use the attribute modifier with state management V2, see Modifier and makeObserved.

examples.title: Example 3: Understanding Custom Modifiers Do Not Support State Data Changes
examples.description: This example shows how to set the width of a custom modifier using state data. Custom modifiers do not support observing changes in data decorated with the @State decorator. Therefore, the width does not change when the button is clicked.

examples.title: Example 4: Combining Modifier and Custom Modifier Attributes
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to set width and height through a custom modifier. When the button is clicked, borderStyle and borderWidth are configured, with all four attributes taking effect simultaneously.

examples.title: Example 5: Setting the Focused State Style with a Modifier
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to implement a focused state style for a Button component by binding it to a modifier. After Button2 is clicked, the Button component displays the focused style when it has focus.

examples.title: Example 6: Setting the Disabled State Style with a Modifier
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to implement a disabled state style for a Button component by binding it to a modifier. After Button2 is clicked, the Button component displays the disabled style when it is disabled.

examples.title: Example 7: Setting the Selected State Style with a Modifier
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to implement a selected state style for a Radio component by binding it to a modifier.

examples.title: Example 8: Implementing the Pressed State Effect for a Custom Component with a Modifier
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to implement a pressed state effect for a custom component (Common) by binding it to a modifier.
